With E011 (−1.2 pp) and E018 (≈−0.7 pp) together, each resolution cut costs about 0.8-1 pp per 10% time. That is worse than epochs, which cost about 0.4-0.5 pp per 10%.

**Measured mechanisms (time, accuracy)**
- Compile + fused SGD: −14% time (E004).

- −0.5 epoch: −4.8% time, −0.2 pp (E008).
- Width 576 → 512: −5% time, −0.4 pp (E010; H1.5.2 is refuted on accuracy).

| Lever | Time |

- With a true margin of about 0.2-0.4 pp, nothing that costs more than about 5% time survives without an accuracy booster.

forecasts.reason: −1 true epoch is −10.5% steps with time proportional to steps, at about −0.45 pp; the −0.5 point H4.2.4 needs is not run, and a single 3-seed difference can't pin the slope.
MACs fall 15.6%, which clears the time bar, but cutting the 8×8-stage width for 100 classes costs about 0.5 pp, and against E016's lucky 0.7607 the loss is more than 1 pp.
Filter wd is inert and scalar wd on the head/BN gives about 0.1 pp; the target, +0.2 pp over E016's 0.7607, is unreachable through noise.
About −7% MACs gives about −6.5% time, short of the 8% bar; losing high-resolution depth costs about 0.3-0.4 pp.
Pixel-weighted compute falls only 3.4%, under the 4% bar; E018 shows low-resolution exposure costs real accuracy, about 0.2 pp here.

cruxes: What is the tip's true 10-seed mean? If it is ≥0.757, about 0.5 epoch of cuts is affordable; if it is ≈0.754, every cut fails and only boosters matter.
Does any time-neutral booster (BN recalibration at 32 px after the EMA swap, an EMA schedule retune, LS scheduling) add ≥0.3 pp? That is the only way to fund the epoch dial.
Does group 2 at 320 channels keep max-autotune kernel efficiency, so that time falls the full ~14% instead of ~8%? That decides whether width beats epochs per pp.
